2. Petitioner case is as Follows:

sentences.text: That on 14.12.2013, petitioner was riding a cycle with a pillion rider in Sadaramangala Road, in front of Joy pee cement godown wherein the driver of the Tempo bearing Reg No.KA-51-7340 drove it, in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused accident.
In the accident petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

He was shifted to Saikrupa Nursing Home,
where he took treatment as inpatient and surgery was conducted and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- for his medical treatment.
3.
Petitioner stated that he was 19 years of age and was working as a mason and was earning Rs.600/- per day,

Further he stated that the accident has occurred due the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the jurisdictional police have registered Cr.No.174/2013 against the driver of the offending vehicle.

He alleged that the Respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he has insured his vehicle with respondent no.1 and accident caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and as such both are liable to pay the compensation with interest and he prayer this tribunal to award the compensation amount by allowing the petition.
4. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, they appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement.

Respondent no.1 being the insurer of vehicle bearing to respondent No.2 contended that the accident occurred due to negligent act of the petitioner and respondent No.2 has violated the permit conditions and the said vehicle was not having fitness certificate as on the date of incident.

Respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle contended that he has insured his vehicle with the respondent No.2 and vehicle was having valid permit and insurance and respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
5. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and examined the doctor as PW.2 produced and marked 17 documents which are at Ex.P.1 to 17 and they are fully cross examined.
6. As per the order dated 03.02.2015, petition is disposed of.

As per the orders passed by the Hon'ble high court of Karnataka in MFA No.6961/2015 (MV-1) order dated 27.03.2024, order passed by this tribunal on 03.02.2015 is set aside and opportunity is extended to the parties herein to lead the further evidence.
7.
In-compliance with aforesaid direction respondent No.2 examined its official as RW-1 produced and marked 5 documents which are at Ex.D1 to 5.
petitioner has not chosen to appear before this tribunal to cross examine the RW-1.

There is no material on record to show that petitioner is prevented from appearing before this tribunal to cross examine the RW-1 and to lead his further evidence in compliance with the direction given by the Hon'ble High court of karnatka.
Considering the conduct and approach of petitioner, cross examination of RW-1 is taken as nil and further evidence of petitioner is taken as nil.

sentences.text: 8. Petitioner and respondents have not chosen to address their arguments orally after obtaining sufficient opportunity from this tribunal.
Considering the age of the petition, both the sides are permitted file their written arguments.
I have perused the entire record.

9. On the basis of pleadings, my learned predecessor in office has framed the following :
ISSUES 1.Whether the petitioner proves that, on 14-12-2013 at about 9.30 a.m. the petitioner was riding the cycle along with pillion rider, slowly on Sadaramangala Road, in front of Jay Pee Cement Godown, at that time one Tempo 709 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, with a high speed and dashed against the petitioner.

Due to this impact petitioner sustained grievous injuries?.
2.Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.What order or award?
10. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
Issue no.1: In the affirmative Issue no.2: In partly affirmative Issue no.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 11. Issue No.1 & 2 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner, he reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.

Petitioner has tender the police records, that is C/copy of FIR, complaint, mahazar, IMV report,
wound certificate, Final report which are at Ex.P.1 to 5.
12.
On careful perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that one Raju Ram S/o mangilal was the driver of the offending vehicle which belongs to the respondent No.2.

The final report filed by the investigating officer which is at Ex.P5, where in the jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle that is tempo 709 involved in the accident.
The aforesaid facts establishes the involvement of the offending vehicle and its driver and his actionable negligent act in the accident.

The final report which is at Ex.P5 is filed after investigation and it is the prima facie proof of the accident and the involvement of the offending vehicle and rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly the police records cannot be doubted and disbelieved.

Gangappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17084510/
3 13.

sentences.text: Petitioner has tender the wound certificate, admission record issued from the Srikrupa Nursing Home, which are at Ex.P.4 and 15, the entry therein shows that the petitioner has sustained fracture of pubic ramie and vertebra and compression on L5 spinal card and he has took conservative treatment for 12 days.
Petitioner has spent Rs.39,595/- for the medical expenses as per Ex.P.13.
Accordingly petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following heads.

14. Pecuniary damages (Medical expenses) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization,
Medicines, Transportation, Nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure:
15.
Petitioner took treatment at Srikrupa hospitals.
Evidently nothing is elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disbelieve the fact that he has sustained the injuries in the alleged accident and he took treatment for the same.
Inasmuch admission report, wound certificate has to be accepted.
Admittedly he has taken treatment for 12 days, for attendant charges, transportation, nourishing food, he might have spend some more expenses.
Therefore in addition to the actual medical expenses of Rs.39,595/- I award Rs.10,000/-.

In total petitioner is entitled for Rs.49,595/-
compensation under this head.
Loss of income during laid up period.
16. The petitioner has not substantiated his nature of work and income as alleged in the petition.
Accident took place in the year 2013, however as per notional income chart, the notional income for the year 2013 is Rs.8,000/-, and same is assessed and considered as his monthly income.
Considering the accidental injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of view that at-least 15 days, he has lost his income.
Therefore I award Rs.8,000/- X 0.5 = Rs.4,000/- as compensation under this head.
Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
17. The petitioner has examined the doctor that is Dr.Rangarajan as PW-2.
He deposed that, he has treated the petitioner and petitioner has 12% of whole body disability.
Learned advocate for the respondent argued that the assessment of PW-2 is on higher side.

I have perused the evidence of PW-2 wound certificate, admission record given by the hospital, X-ray etc.
18.
Evidently PW-2 has not tender the details of his assessment regarding whole body disability of the petitioner.
Admittedly petitioner has no functional disability.
It is true that petitioner sustained the grievous injuries and he has not undergone surgery, further doctor has admitted that the fracture is united.
Petitioner has not placed any acceptable evidence to believe that he has spent some money for followup treatment.

Considering the medical reports and oral testimony of doctor,
the whole body disability of the petitioner is assessed as 10%.
19. The notional monthly income of the petitioner is assessed as Rs.8,000/-, the age of petitioner as on the date of accident is 19 years as per the medical records.
The multiplier applicable to this case is "18".

Therefore loss of income on account of permanent disability is calculated as follows;
Gangappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17084510/
4 Rs.8,000/-(Monthly income) X 12 (Months) X 18 ( Multiplier) X10% (Functional Disability) =
Rs.1,72,800/-

entities.text: Gangappa vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the petitioner is entitle for Rs.1,72,800/- as compensation under this head.

Non-Pecuniary damages (General damages) (IV)Damages for pain and sufferings and loss of amenities:
20.
It is undisputed fact that petitioner has sustained grievous injury and it is grievous in nature.
During the hospitalization and rehabilitation period, he might have undergone lot of pain and sufferings and due to accidental injuries he has forgone certain amenities available for him.
There fore I award Rs.5,000/- under these conventional heads.

V) Loss of Amenities :-
21.
The petitioner has to forego certain amenities available for him before accident.
Therefore I award Rs.5,000/- as compensation under this head.
22. Except these heads the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under any other heads.
In all the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Sl Particulars Amount  No.
 1

Pecuniary damages Rs.49,595/-
 2 Loss of income during the laid up period Rs. 4,000/-

3 Loss of income on account of Rs.1,72,800/-
 permanent disability

4 pain & sufferings Rs. 5,000/-
 5 loss of amenities Rs. 5,000/-
 6 TOTAL Rs.2,36,395/-
23. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
24. Liability:

The insurance company has not disputed the validity of the policy of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, respondent No.1 has failed to prove the contention that is insured has violated the permit conditions.
Ex.R2 is the certified copy of the permit issued to offending vehicle and it is valid as on the date of the accident.
It is bounded duty of the insurer to verify the permit conditions of the vehicle before issuing the insurance coverage for the same.

Accordingly Respondent No.1 is the liable to pay the compensation amount and respondent No.1 is directed to deposit compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
Hence with the aforesaid discussion based on the evidence placed on record, Accordingly I am answering Issue No.1 the affirmative and issue No.2 in partly affirmative.

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor vehicle Act,1988, is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioner is entitled for the compensation amount of Rs.2,36,395/- with interest at the rate of 6% P.A from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this tribunal with in 30 days from the date of the judgment.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, office is directed to release the entire amount to the petitioner through K2, after compliance of mandate of circular No.39/2020 dated 17.01.2020.
Advocate fee of Rs.1000/- is fixed.
All the interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
